name: projectionist
description: Home media pipeline for a Synology NAS: renames, notes, subtitles, posters, collections, Plex/Jellyfin sync (Go, Docker)

readme.html:
projectionist

A home media server's upkeep, done by one Go service. projectionist runs in one container on a Synology NAS beside Plex and Jellyfin. It keeps the film and TV library tidy: it names files, finds and times subtitles, picks posters, builds collections, keeps watch history in step across both apps, and checks the apps' health. Before it, the same work was a set of Python scripts: DSM's task scheduler ran some of them, and the others ran by hand. Each script is ported as a stage, checked against the script's own output, and deleted at its cutover. Some stages are new.

The name comes from the person in the booth: a projectionist runs the show and stays out of the audience's way. Here that is a hard rule. A job that moves or re-encodes files pauses while anyone but the owner is watching.

The stages

A stage is one job with one interface (Name(), Run(ctx, env, *Report) error). It must be idempotent: a rerun after a crash finishes the work and never repeats a side effect. Each stage runs on its own schedule. A stage runs only when its [stages.<name>] table in the config enables it.

Stage What it does
watcher Watches the library folders with inotify. When a new folder has been quiet for 3 minutes, it triggers the stages that act on it. A 15-minute sweep catches lost events.
rename Keeps Movies/ and TV/ in one naming scheme. Identity comes from the file names and TMDB, never from Plex or Jellyfin. Every move is one atomic renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE), written to an undo log before it happens.
details Keeps a small text note beside each video (codec, HDR, audio and subtitle tracks), from ffprobe.
subtitles Finds English subtitles for videos that have none. The cheap routes come first: an embedded English track, or a subtitle made for the same release. Next, a subtitle is timed against four short windows of the video. Full alignment (alass) runs only at night, and only while nobody else is watching. OCR reads subtitle tracks that are only images.
posters Picks a poster for each title from TMDB and fanart.tv. A vision model judges the candidates, under a hard spending cap. The owner's own uploads are never replaced.
collections Keeps film collections (franchises, directors) the same in Plex and Jellyfin.
lists Mirrors film canon lists (for example, Letterboxd's Top 500, the Criterion Collection, Sight and Sound) as collections, in list order.
letterboxd Reads Letterboxd diaries into the watch record, and Letterboxd watchlists into each user's Plex watchlist.
jfsync Keeps watched state, progress and ratings the same in Plex and Jellyfin. It writes from projectionist's own watch record, which webhooks and one-time imports fill.
tonight Each day, gives each person a "Tonight" shelf of five films from the library they have not seen: films over a Letterboxd and Rotten Tomatoes bar (MDBList's ratings), shuffled, or (mode = "recommend") ranked by their taste. No model call.
remote4k Makes small 4K copies (hardware HEVC) of the films on a "Remote 4K" list, for streaming away from home. The encode is paused with SIGSTOP while someone else watches.
gpu-guard Keeps Plex's hardware transcoding on the integrated GPU. It repairs drift, alerts once on each CPU transcode, and runs a GPU self-test once a day when the box is idle.
health Probes Plex, Jellyfin and the containers every 5 minutes. It restarts a hung Jellyfin only when nobody is playing on it. When Plex's Movies tab gets slow, it runs Plex's database optimize at night.
audit A read-only library audit: names outside the scheme, unreadable videos, orphan sidecar files, identical copies.
appbackup Makes nightly versions of the app databases on the NVMe volume: SQLite's online backup, plus hardlinks for unchanged files.

Architecture

                         Synology NAS (DSM 7.4, Intel J4125 + UHD 600)
 ┌──────────────────────── container "projectionist" (host network) ────────────────────────┐
 │                                                                                          │
 │  scheduler ── one goroutine per stage; cadence + optional window (e.g. 01:00-07:00);     │
 │      │        never two copies of a stage at once                                        │
 │      ▼                                                                                   │
 │  Runner ── StartRun ─► stage.Run(ctx, env, &report) ─► FinishRun(outcome) ─► logs        │
 │      │                       │                                                           │
 │      │     watcher · rename · details · subtitles · posters · collections · lists        │
 │      │     letterboxd · jfsync · tonight · remote4k · gpu-guard · health · audit         │
 │      │     appbackup                                                                     │
 │      │                                                                                   │
 │      │   env: Plex · Jellyfin · TMDB · fanart.tv · LLM clients · viewers.Gate (pause     │
 │      │        rule) · probe (ffprobe cache) · fsx (renameat2, FICLONE, dir fsync)        │
 │      ▼                                                                                   │
 │  SQLite /state/projectionist.db (WAL): runs · kv · events · probe_cache · <stage>_*      │
 │  HTTP on loopback :8097: GET /health (503 on an alert) · GET /metrics (Prometheus)       │
 └──────┬──────────────────┬──────────────────────┬──────────────────────┬──────────────────┘
        │ /dev/dri         │ HTTP, loopback       │ /volume1/media       │ read-only:
        │ renderD128       │                      │ (the only rw mount)  │ Plex app data
        ▼                  ▼                      ▼                      ▼
   GPU (QSV/VAAPI)    Plex · Jellyfin       Movies/ TV/ _archive/    Preferences.xml (token)

   DSM scheduled task: curl -fsS <loopback>:8097/health every 15 min → DSM's failure e-mail

The design rules that shape the code:

  • Plex and Jellyfin are sinks, not sources. Facts come from the files (ffprobe, names, rename logs) and from TMDB. The apps receive writes and report who is watching. Both apps stall during library scans, so every call to them has a deadline, and a slow app never fails a run.
  • State lives in SQLite. Every run is a row. A stage that a restart cut off resumes from its own state. The next run time comes from the last start time, so a restart does not run a stage early.
  • Measured file system facts. On the NAS's btrfs, renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE) and FICLONE reflinks work, also across shares. chmod strips a Synology ACL, but chown keeps it. So no stage ever calls chmod. The rename executor does one fsync per unit, not one per operation.
  • Port, compare, delete. A stage replaced a script only when it matched the script's output on a gate. For example, the rename planner matched the Python planner on 21,333 of 21,334 recorded rows, and the one difference was intended. The old script went away in the same cutover.

docs/architecture.md has the full design, each stage's gate and the measurements. docs/STAGES.md records the status of each stage and its evidence.

How it runs on the NAS

  • One image, no registry. make save builds a linux/amd64 image and writes a tarball. On the NAS, docker load reads it, and a Container Manager project runs compose.yaml. The image holds the static Go binary (about 16 MB, stripped), the same ffmpeg build that Jellyfin uses (with the Intel QSV/VAAPI drivers), alass, and a two small helpers on ONNX Runtime: cmd/subocr (OCR, a PP-OCR text model) and cmd/subvad (speech, Silero VAD).
  • Host network, hardware encode. The container shares the host network to reach Plex and Jellyfin on loopback. /dev/dri/renderD128 is passed through for QSV encodes.
  • Least privilege. The service runs as root inside the container, so that files it moves keep their owners. All capabilities are dropped except six: CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE and FOWNER for the library files, and SETUID, SETGID and KILL to run (and stop) Plex's transcoder as the Plex user for the GPU self-test. The root file system is read-only, no-new-privileges is set, memory is capped at 1 GB, and cpu_shares: 256 lets Plex and Jellyfin win any contention. The media share is the only writable media mount.
  • Secrets are files. API keys arrive as compose secrets under /run/secrets/ and are read on each request, so a rotated key needs no restart. Plex's token is read from its Preferences.xml (a read-only mount). No secret is in an environment variable, the config, a URL or a log line.
  • Alerts use what was already there. /health answers 503 while any stage has an open alert. A one-line DSM task curls it every 15 minutes, and DSM's own failure e-mail is the alert channel. /metrics exports runs, alerts, items and durations per stage.
  • One stage by hand. projectionist run <stage> -config FILE runs one stage once and exits 1 on an alert or an error. projectionist check -config FILE validates the config as serve would and starts nothing: run it before a restart.

Configure it for your home

Everything that belongs to one household lives in one config file, never in the code: the people and their Plex, Jellyfin and Letterboxd accounts, the NAS paths, the Plex library ids, the collection and playlist names, the hours the heavy work may run. To run projectionist at home, copy config.example.toml to /config/projectionist.toml, replace its placeholders (your-plex-username, your-letterboxd-username, media.example.com, /volume1/media, ...), delete the tables of the stages you do not want, and put your API keys in the secret files compose mounts at /run/secrets/. Then build the image (make image, or make save for a tarball to docker load), run projectionist check -config /config/projectionist.toml in it, and start the Container Manager project. The check names every missing or wrong key as section.key with what to set, and serve refuses to start until there are none. docs/configuration.md lists every parameter, its default and an example, the secret files, and a minimal working config. A deployment keeps its own config outside git; in a checkout, deploy/nas/ holds a copy and git ignores it.

Build and test

Requires Go 1.26. Docker is needed only for test-linux and the image.

make test        # go test ./...
make vet         # go vet for the host and for linux/amd64
make test-linux  # the tests in a golang:1.26 container (the renameat2 and FICLONE paths)
make build       # static linux/amd64 binary in bin/
make image       # the container image (docker buildx, linux/amd64)
make save        # the image as a tarball, for docker load on the NAS

The tests use fake Plex, Jellyfin, TMDB and model servers (internal/fake, internal/llm/llmtest), stand-in ffmpeg and ffprobe scripts, and a fake clock, so they need no accounts, keys or media. Harnesses that replay real NAS data are behind build tags (replay, calibrate, gate) and do not run by default.

To add a stage, see docs/SKELETON_READY.md.

Layout

Path Contents
cmd/projectionist The service: serve, run <stage>, check, align-worker
cmd/subocr OCR helper for image subtitle tracks
cmd/subvad Speech helper: the stretches Silero VAD hears as speech, for subtitle alignment
cmd/bakeoff Compares vision models as poster judges, to pick the one the posters stage uses
internal/stage, internal/scheduler, internal/store The stage interface, the scheduler and the SQLite state
internal/stages/<name> One package per stage
internal/plex, jellyfin, tmdb, fanart, llm The API clients
internal/viewers The pause rule
internal/fsx, internal/probe Atomic file operations and the ffprobe cache
config/ The collection lists the collections stage reads
testdata/ The synthetic config the tests share (roles and example.com hosts, no real people)
deploy/nas/ Not in git: the NAS's own compose file and config, copied after each deploy

Licence

MIT. See LICENSE. The container image also bundles third-party binaries (jellyfin-ffmpeg, alass, ONNX Runtime and a PP-OCR model), each under its own licence.
